name: Psychology
notes: Encodes the NEW psychology major (students matriculating Fall 2025 and beyond). Earlier matriculants follow the retiring major (same intro/stat; PSYC 110+111 both required; two social-science core from 161/170-171/180/281; different elective count).
An AP psychology score of 4 or 5 waives PSYC 101.
Statistics should be completed by end of sophomore year; statistics is a prerequisite for research methods (take methods by end of junior year).
Cross-listed pairs (PSYC 110/BCSC 110, PSYC 111/BCSC 111, NSCI 201/BCSC 240) count once - not auto-enforced.
Elective caps not auto-enforced: no more than eight credits of independent research/study (39X) or teaching courses (PSYC 301-304, 390).

requirementGroups.label: Introductory course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One Introductory Course: PSYC 101: Intro to Psychology (an AP psychology test score of 4 or 5 will waive this requirement)

requirementGroups.label: Statistics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose one of the following: STAT 180 ... (formerly STAT 212); STAT 190 ... (formerly STAT 213); STAT 203: Introduction to Mathematical Statistics

requirementGroups.label: Research methods
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose one of the following: PSYC 218: Research Methods in Psychology (lecture-based version); PSYC 219W: Research Methods in Psychology (hands-on experience version)

requirementGroups.label: Cognitive & neurobiological foundations (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose two of the following: PSYC 110/BCSC 110: Neural Foundations of Behavior or NSCI 201/BCSC 240: Basic Neurobiology; PSYC 111/BCSC 111: Foundations of Cognitive Science; PSYC 112: Social, Affective, and Clinical Neuroscience
requirementGroups.note: Cross-listed/either-or pairs count as one choice; the app lists all codes for placement flexibility.

requirementGroups.label: Social, developmental & clinical foundations (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose two of the following: PSYC 161: Social Psychology and Individual Differences; PSYC 170: Child Development; PSYC 180: Intro to Psychopathology

requirementGroups.label: Psychology electives (5)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students must complete five, four-credit elective courses in PSYC. ... No more than eight credits can be independent research/study courses or teaching courses.

upperLevelWriting.label: Two PSYC upper-level writing courses (at least one at 200+)
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: Students are required to take two of their psychology courses designated as upper-level writing courses, and at least one of these courses is to be at or above the 200 level.
upperLevelWriting.note: Half-credit W tagalong sections, PSYC 39X with faculty approval, and WRTG 274/PSYC 274W also qualify; the at-least-one-200+ rule is not auto-enforced.
